solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Go round the world in MCC tour I've again organised, missing nothing

indicators.note: letters that are organised are put into a new order, so the fodder is rearranged
missing tells us to drop something from the fodder before rearranging it

parts.note: these words supply the letters to be rearranged, once the O is taken out
nothing is zero, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A cricket club's touring party plans another trip around the globe.
explanation.walkthrough: MCC is the Marylebone Cricket Club, which sends England cricket teams on tour, so the surface reads as sports news.
explanation.definitionFit: To circumnavigate is to sail or travel all the way around something, classically the globe.

clue.text: Diminish captain's position in game

parts.note: to contract is to shrink or diminish
a ship's captain stands on the bridge

explanation.surface: A sports report about cutting back the captain's role in a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Contract bridge is the standard modern form of the card game played by four players in pairs.

clue.text: Raced around area, infuriated, in fast time

indicators.note: around means the raced word wraps the next letters

parts.note: ran is the past tense of run, meaning raced
mad means angry

explanation.surface: An angry runner dashes around a district during a period of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramadan is the Islamic month of fasting from dawn to dusk, a time of the year.

clue.text: Pressured to wear informal clothing outside university

indicators.note: outside means the clothing verb goes around the university letter

parts.note: to underdress is to dress more casually than the occasion demands

explanation.surface: Someone is pushed into turning up casual outside a college campus.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting under duress means acting under threat or compulsion, that is, pressured into it.

clue.text: Delicious drink in the neighbourhood around court

indicators.note: around means the neighbourhood word goes about the court letters

parts.note: near means close by

explanation.surface: A tasty beverage is sold somewhere close to the courthouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar was the drink of the gods in mythology, and the word now praises any delightful beverage.

clue.text: Check restraining macho types getting heated

indicators.note: restraining means the check word holds the macho types inside

parts.note: to vet is to check or examine
he-men are strongly masculine men

explanation.surface: A checkpoint holds back some tough guys who are getting angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehement means forceful and passionate, as in a heated argument.

clue.text: Admirable person repeatedly contributing to stage management

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the phrase, and occurs a second time within the second word as well

parts.note: the letters run across the end of stage and the start of management, and appear again inside management

explanation.surface: A treasured colleague who keeps chipping in to run the theatre backstage.
explanation.walkthrough: The three letters straddle the two words, and appear again inside the second word, hence repeatedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a gem means they are a treasure, a very fine and valued individual.

clue.text: Revolutionary movement adjusting without monarch

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the adjusting word goes around the monarch

parts.note: tuning an engine or instrument is adjusting it
R is short for rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: A political uprising reforms itself after getting rid of the king.
explanation.walkthrough: Without looks like removal, but in its older sense it means outside, so the monarch letter goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheel turning makes a rotating motion, a revolution, so turning is literally revolutionary movement.

clue.text: Adventurously moving piece, rushed attempt to capture queen

indicators.note: the knight takes the queen, standing next to it

parts.note: a knight is a chess piece
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
ran means rushed
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A chess move: a knight's hasty bid to take the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, for Elizabeth Regina, is a standard way to clue a queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Knight-errantry was the medieval practice of knights roaming the land in search of adventure.

clue.text: Unusual CD I am on, always moving?

indicators.note: unusual suggests the letters are in an odd, unexpected order and must be rearranged

parts.note: these words are taken letter for letter as the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a strange compact disc is permanently playing on their stereo.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic peoples have no fixed home and travel from place to place, hence the question mark on a loose description.

clue.text: Poet leading international group, as result of big hit in US

definitions.text: result of big hit in US

indicators.note: leading means the poet comes in front of the next piece

parts.note: Homer is the ancient Greek poet of the Iliad and Odyssey
the UN, the United Nations

explanation.surface: A poet heads a global body, which reads like a headline about a celebrity appointment.
explanation.walkthrough: A home run in baseball is the reward for hitting the ball out of the park, which is why US is in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball a hit that clears the field lets the batter circle all the bases and score, called a home run.

clue.text: Off colour?

definitions.meaning: in the surface, off colour means feeling unwell; read cryptically, off means not one of
in snooker the coloured balls are called colours, as distinct from the fifteen balls of one other kind

explanation.walkthrough: In snooker, players pot a red and then a colour; the reds are explicitly not counted among the colours, so a red is literally not a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Snooker terminology separates the reds from the six colours, so the ball named here is outside the colour category.

clue.text: Hand in scholarship that's again providing entry

indicators.note: in places the hand piece inside the scholarship word

parts.note: reading, as in a person of wide reading, means learning or scholarship
mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: A student submits an essay that gains them admission once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Readmitting someone means letting them in again, giving them entry a second time.

clue.text: Discoverer of stars having latest count wrong

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters are in the incorrect order and need rearranging

parts.note: these two words are taken letter for letter as the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: An astronomer with a miscounted tally of new stars.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests astronomy, but the stars are performers.
explanation.definitionFit: A talent scout spots promising performers who may become celebrities, that is, stars.

clue.text: Agree with Conservative about despicable type

parts.note: on means about, as in a book on birds
a cur is a mongrel dog, and by extension a contemptible person

explanation.surface: Someone sides with a Tory politician on the subject of a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur is to be of the same opinion, a formal synonym for agreeing.

clue.text: Running one kind of entertainment

definitions.meaning: first meaning: fleeing, on the run
second meaning: the films and music offered to passengers on a plane

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses of one hyphenated phrase: running away, and the sort of entertainment shown on an airliner.
explanation.definitionFit: Fugitives are said to be in flight, and airlines advertise their in-flight entertainment.

clue.text: Person operating over time as supplier of delicacy

indicators.note: over means the operating person spreads across, covering the time letter

parts.note: a surgeon carries out operations

explanation.surface: A surgeon working overtime to provide a fine treat.
explanation.definitionFit: The sturgeon is the fish whose roe is caviar, a luxury food.

clue.text: Colour of hair improved when cut with streak put in

indicators.note: put in places the streak inside the shortened word
cut tells us to chop off the last letter

parts.note: something improved is better
a run, like a winning streak, is a series of successes

explanation.surface: A hairdresser's note: hair colour looks better after a trim and some highlights.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunette describes dark brown hair, so it names a hair shade.

clue.text: Cook for short time that's rounded off

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of rounded are rearranged

parts.note: the word is taken letter for letter as the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: A cookery instruction about briefly heating something that has been shaped and finished.
explanation.definitionFit: To underdo food is to cook it less than fully, so it is cooked only briefly.

clue.text: Not just dark, also raining perhaps?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: read as not fair, which describes dark hair and also bad weather

explanation.walkthrough: Fair means just, blonde and dry weather, so the negative covers all three: unjust, dark-haired and rainy.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfair literally means not fair, and fair has senses of justice, pale colouring and fine weather.

clue.text: What's contained in shot in local drunk?

definitions.text: What's contained in shot in local drunk?

indicators.note: in places the inner letters of shot inside the rearranged word
drunk suggests the letters are reeling and out of order

parts.note: the word, meaning a pub in the surface, is taken letter for letter to be rearranged

indicators.note: the letters contained in the word, leaving off its outer letters

parts.note: the inner two letters of the word, losing its first and last

explanation.surface: A question about what fills a shot glass at a pub with tipsy drinkers.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot is a small measure of spirits, and spirits are alcoholic drink, especially in a pub full of drunks.

clue.text: Bonnie and Clyde, say, left in American car

indicators.note: in places the left letter inside the car

parts.note: a coupe is a two-door car, the American spelling without the accent

explanation.surface: The outlaw lovers abandoned in a getaway car.
explanation.walkthrough: Bonnie and Clyde were a 1930s American outlaw pair who famously died in their car.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonnie and Clyde were a romantic partnership, an example of a pair of lovers.

clue.text: Diligent musical group ahead of us on river

indicators.note: in an across answer, on means placed after the river
ahead of puts the group before us

parts.note: the Indus is a major river flowing through Pakistan
a trio is a group of three musicians
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hard-working band arrives at the riverside before we do.
explanation.definitionFit: Industrious people work hard and steadily, the same quality as being diligent.

clue.text: From taps, initially, a drink

parts.note: taps are marked with initials: C for cold and H for hot

explanation.surface: Making a drink straight from the taps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' here means the initials printed on the taps, not the first letter of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cha is British slang for tea, the drink.

clue.text: Relevant as a new drug after what causes illness

indicators.note: after places the following letters behind the illness piece

parts.note: a germ is a microbe that causes disease
taken as written
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A doctor's remark that a novel medicine following an infection is pertinent.
explanation.definitionFit: Germane means pertinent or bearing on the subject, a close synonym of relevant.

clue.text: Player who excels in matches, ignoring the odds

indicators.note: ignoring the odd-numbered letters keeps only the second, fourth and sixth letters

parts.note: the word whose even-placed letters, second, fourth and sixth, are kept

explanation.surface: A star performer who wins games against the bookmakers' predictions.
explanation.definitionFit: An ace is an expert, a top performer in a sport or skill.

clue.text: Visionary's other novel covering page after page

indicators.note: page after page puts one page in front of the rest
covering means the rearranged letters wrap around a page
novel means new or different, so the word other is rearranged

parts.note: the word is taken letter for letter as the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: A dreamer's second book wraps its story across page after page.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophet foresees the future, so is a visionary in the sense of a seer.

clue.text: Travel with French writer mostly in mind to see how countries are run

definitions.text: to see how countries are run

parts.note: to go is to travel

indicators.note: mostly means take most of the word, dropping its last letter

parts.note: Jules Verne, French author of Around the World in Eighty Days
mentally means in the mind

explanation.surface: A writer travels with a famous French novelist in their thoughts, observing the governments of the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking at something governmentally means from the standpoint of government, how states are administered.
